Keywords: Only, Coming, Bringing

outputs.L1:

Coming home from the daily race,

outputs.L2:
An ordinary father, weary from the day,  
Returns from work with little wealth or praise  
To prove how well he has met life’s demands.  
Yet happiness fills him when his family delights  
In his arrival and the sound of his voice.  

A simple father raising children four,  
One among more than ten million men,  
He presses onward through the daily struggle,  
Enduring life’s cruelty and contempt  
Without a murmur of suffering or resentment,  
All for the loved ones waiting at home.  

He is just a father—not wealthy or boastful—  
Only another figure in the restless multitude,  
Laboring and persevering one day after another,  
Prepared to confront whatever lies ahead.  
When bitter judgments fall, he remains quiet,  
Accepting every burden because he loves them.  

He may be only a father, but he sacrifices everything  
To make life easier for his young children.  
With firm and somber courage, he carries out  
The same loving duties his own father performed for him.  
And so I write these words in his honor:  
He is merely a dad, yet the finest of men.
outputs.L3:
After a long and exhausting day at work, a weary father returns home. The burdens of the day still weigh upon him, but they begin to fade when he sees the happiness on his family’s faces. Their warm welcome reminds him why he works so hard and gives him the strength to face another day.

He is an ordinary man—neither wealthy nor famous. The world may never recognize his efforts or praise his achievements, yet he quietly endures life’s hardships for the sake of those who depend on him. He bears responsibility without seeking attention, finding purpose in providing security and comfort for his family.

At times, he faces criticism, disappointment, and adversity. Still, he rarely complains. His love for his family keeps him steady, allowing him to meet each challenge with patience and courage. Even when life is difficult, he continues forward because he knows that others rely on his strength.

He gives everything he can to make life easier and brighter for his children. In doing so, he follows the example of his own father, carrying forward a legacy of duty, sacrifice, and unconditional love. His greatest hope is not personal success, but the happiness and well-being of those he loves.

He may think of himself as “only a dad,” but there is nothing small about his devotion. His quiet courage, constant sacrifice, and steadfast love reveal the true measure of his character. Though he may never receive public praise, to his family he is more than an ordinary man—he is one of the very best.
outputs.L4:
The poem presents the father as an ordinary, hardworking man whose greatness lies not in wealth, status, or public recognition, but in his steady devotion to his family. Through repeated images of labor, hardship, and daily struggle, the poet emphasizes the difficult life he endures. His sacrifices are quiet and often unnoticed: he bears physical exhaustion, financial pressure, and personal disappointment without complaint so that his children may enjoy greater comfort and better opportunities.

Although the father possesses little in material terms, he gives his family everything he can. His strength is revealed through patience, perseverance, and an unwavering sense of responsibility. Rather than seeking praise, he expresses love through practical acts—working, providing, protecting, and easing the burdens of those who depend on him. The repetition of these ordinary sacrifices gives them emotional power, showing that heroism can be found in the routines of everyday life.

Ultimately, the poem redefines greatness. The father may never become rich or famous, yet his selflessness gives his life profound dignity and meaning. By placing his children’s needs before his own and continuing to endure hardship for their sake, he becomes a deeply admirable figure. His quiet love and sacrifice form a lasting legacy, suggesting that true greatness is measured not by what a person possesses, but by how much they are willing to give.
outputs.L5:
**Only Coming, Bringing**

Only when the night grows quiet do we hear the future coming. It arrives without fanfare, bringing new hopes, unexpected challenges, and the possibility of change. We cannot know exactly what it will carry, but we can choose how to welcome it—with courage, curiosity, and an open heart.

counterfactuals.output:
**The Quiet Strength of Father**

He rises before the morning light,  
With weary hands and purpose bright.  
No praise he seeks, no thanks demands—  
He builds our world with calloused hands.

He carries burdens, deep and wide,  
Yet keeps the ache of life inside.  
Through every storm, through every trial,  
He shields our hearts and wears a smile.

His dreams are tucked behind our own,  
His love in every seed he’s sown.  
He gives his time, his strength, his all,  
And stands beside us when we fall.

Though humble words may leave him unsung,  
His faithful story lives among  
The lives he shaped, the hopes he grew—  
A thousand quiet acts of love made true.

Dear Father, may you always know  
How deeply your devotion shows.  
You are the root, the guiding light,  
Our steady dawn, our strength at night.

And if we stand both proud and tall,  
It’s because you gave to us your all.
